title: Platform-bypass motive scan
purpose: Determine why actors knowingly leave mature transaction platforms for WeChat/direct/off-platform deals. Retain only if the bypass is caused by an unresolved transaction-unit/availability/acceptance/replacement failure that a Rooter control plane can remove while retaining recurring value.
scan_rule: DIRECT REPEAT RELATIONSHIP != DEMAND FOR A HEAVIER INTERMEDIARY
Off-platform risk can strengthen incumbent platform protection rather than create a new routing layer.
A candidate requires evidence that users bypass because the platform transaction unit itself fails even when fee pressure is low.

observed_behavior: A 2026 freight case records a driver proposing WeChat/off-platform settlement to a shipper under the stated rationale of easier detail coordination and saving platform fees.
The shipper accepted because both sides expected lower cost.
failure_after_bypass: The platform service fee had already been charged at order access, so the claimed saving was misleading.
The off-platform move reduced transaction protection and became part of a serious cargo-risk event.
patterns_tested.meaning: Bypass was not evidence that a new router was needed; incumbent platform monitoring/protection had positive value.

patterns_tested.observed_behavior: Current platform rules explicitly define and govern merchants inducing users to cancel/avoid platform transactions and pay by cash, Alipay, WeChat or other off-platform channels.
patterns_tested.meaning: Flying orders are sufficiently common to require formal anti-bypass rules, but the rule itself does not show platform incapability.

patterns_tested.observed_behavior: Current private-domain software explicitly markets moving platform food-delivery customers into WeChat/self-operated ordering.
stated_motive: reduce platform commission and promotion cost
retain repeat customers in owned private-domain channels
patterns_tested.meaning: The bypass product is itself designed around fee reduction and customer ownership, not an unsolved routing/acceptance problem.

observed_pressure: Current reporting shows some maintenance platforms can impose very high effective platform shares in certain service categories.
High platform take can compress technician income and contribute to off-platform add-on pricing or independent work.
counterevidence: The market already contains multiple guaranteed/escrow platforms.
The market also contains zero- or low-commission alternatives, including platforms that explicitly advertise no commission or current technician commission exemption.
Therefore high commission is a competitive platform-pricing problem, not a missing Rooter function.

observed_behavior: Machining communities and platforms can provide free/zero-commission demand publication and supplier discovery.
Current machining platforms advertise 0 transaction commission for buyers and very large factory networks.
patterns_tested.why_it_matters: If participants still prefer direct contact, commission avoidance alone cannot justify building another marketplace; direct relationship itself is part of the desired transaction model.

observed_behavior: Some current platforms explicitly advertise technician no-commission or zero-commission models while retaining matching/order tooling.
Other mature platforms provide escrow, monitoring, warranty and dispute handling.
patterns_tested.result: No current evidence was bound showing users systematically leave these low/no-commission platforms because of a specific unresolved micro-unit, live-availability, acceptance or replacement defect.

material_learning: Platform bypass often expresses economic disintermediation rather than demand for a better intermediary.
Where users primarily avoid fees or preserve direct repeat relationships, transaction-commission Rooter economics are structurally weak.
Off-platform fraud/risk events can increase the value of incumbent platform protection rather than reveal a new neutral layer.
Low/no-commission alternatives already exist in several service and manufacturing markets, yet no current non-fee bypass residual was bound.
cross_industry_result.current_best_next_truth: Fresh Scan 019 should invert the search: find current markets where buyer and supplier already know each other yet continue paying a middle layer repeatedly. Persistent voluntary payment after direct contact is evidence of non-bypassable value. Identify what the intermediary owns—availability, liability, acceptance, financing, replacement, compliance, aggregation or settlement—and search for a smaller Xuzhou/Jiangsu market where the same value exists informally but is not yet owned by a mature incumbent.
